mainTopic: אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב: the widow and slave cases, and what counts as the price of a dog
overview: The גמרא first explains that the source forbidding a widow's payment from a כהן גדול follows רבי אלעזר. It shows that the widow case teaches something new: even payment for a relationship the תורה forbids is אתנן. Next it discusses the משנה about a lamb given so that a maidservant will be with 'my slave'. רב הונא reads 'slave' as a polite word for the master himself. שמואל בר רב יצחק instead says the case is about a real עבד עברי. When the גמרא asks how the חכמים can then forbid it, it answers that the slave has no wife and children, and the משנה's dispute depends on that. Then a new משנה defines מחיר כלב as an animal traded for a dog. It adds that the swapped cases and the offspring are permitted. The גמרא proves from the פסוק's wording that מחיר means a trade, and explains why all ten lambs in the partners case are forbidden. Finally it quotes the ruling that אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה are permitted, and רבא מפרזקיא begins a question to רב אשי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The source follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The earlier source that forbids the payment follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that any relationship not for marriage makes a woman a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This source is the view of רבי אלעזר, who says: an unmarried man who is with an unmarried woman, not for the sake of marriage, has made her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says which תנא the earlier source follows: רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר has a very wide definition of זונה. Even a woman who is with an unmarried man outside of marriage counts. That is why, by his view, her payment is forbidden as אתנן for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: An unmarried man / an unmarried woman
A woman with the status of a harlot
Payment to a זונה, which may not be brought as an offering

phrases.english: It is the view of Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the source discussed just before, which forbids a widow's payment from a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: who says: an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman
not for the sake of marriage
has made her a zonah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section by identifying the author of the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to state a law that everyone accepts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source follows רבי אלעזר's wide definition of זונה.

steps.title: Why mention a widow and not any unmarried woman
steps.stepSummary: If the source follows רבי אלעזר, it should have used the simpler case of any unmarried woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי אלעזר, why specifically a widow? Let it teach an unmarried woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי אלעזר, even an ordinary unmarried woman's payment is forbidden. So why did the source choose the narrower case of a widow with a כהן גדול? The broader case would have taught more.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow (forbidden to a כהן גדול)

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Elazar,
why specifically a widow?
Let it teach an unmarried woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, מַאי אִירְיָא אַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the widow case in a source that follows רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אלעזר the broader case of a פנויה already forbids the payment, so the widow case seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The widow case was needed to teach something new
steps.stepSummary: Without the widow case, one might think that only the model case (a פנויה) makes the payment forbidden, and not a relationship the תורה forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: The widow case was necessary. You might have thought: since the unmarried woman is the model case, payments for forbidden relationships are not prohibited. So the source teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the widow case teaches something we would not have known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a פנויה is the בנין אב, the model for the law of אתנן. One might think the law applies only to relationships like that one, which the תורה does not forbid. The widow and כהן גדול case shows that even when the relationship is forbidden by the תורה, the payment is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The model case from which a rule is learned

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי אלעזר, the payment is forbidden both for an ordinary unmarried woman and for a relationship the תורה forbids, like a widow with a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: The widow was necessary,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since it is the model case,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the unmarried woman case, which the rule of אתנן is modeled on.

phrases.english: they should not be prohibited,
phrases.notes: 'They' means payments for relationships the תורה forbids.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the case is needed to teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פנויה is the model case, payments for relationships the תורה forbids would not be prohibited.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even payments for relationships the תורה forbids are prohibited as אתנן.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the lamb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about someone who gives a lamb so that the other's maidservant will be with his slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says to his fellow: 'Here is this lamb for you,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, someone gives a lamb so that his friend's maidservant will be with 'my slave'. רבי says the lamb is not אתנן, and the חכמים say it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: One who says to his fellow
"Here is this lamb for you," etc.
phrases.notes: The full case continues: in return, your maidservant will be with my slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ הֵא לָךְ טָלֶה זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case of a lamb given in exchange for a maidservant being with a slave; רבי and the חכמים disagree whether it is אתנן.

steps.title: A maidservant is permitted to a slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים would call it אתנן, since a maidservant is allowed to be with a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a maidservant is permitted to a slave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שפחה כנענית is permitted to an עבד כנעני. If the relationship is permitted, this is not זנות. So why would the חכמים say the lamb is forbidden as אתנן?

phrases.english: But a maidservant to a slave
is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים' ruling in the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' ruling that the lamb is אתנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A permitted relationship cannot produce אתנן, and a maidservant is permitted to a slave.

steps.title: 'My slave' is a polite way of saying 'me'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the master really means the maidservant will be with him. The word 'slave' is just a polite way of saying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: He means 'with him', and when it says 'slave', it is using a polite way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by reading the משנה differently: the man is really paying for the maidservant to be with himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man himself is with the maidservant, that is a forbidden relationship, so the payment can be אתנן. The משנה said 'my slave' only to avoid saying something unpleasant directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A nice, polite way of speaking

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'slave' does not mean a real slave. רב הונא says it is a polite word for the master himself.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
He means "with him,"
and as for what it teaches, "slave" —
it is speaking in a polite way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's wording as a polite phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a real slave, which would be a permitted relationship.
steps.terutzMaskana: The master is paying for the maidservant to be with himself, a forbidden relationship.

steps.title: Then why does רבי permit the lamb
steps.stepSummary: If the man is paying for a forbidden relationship with himself, why does רבי say the lamb is not אתנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is רבי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's answer from the other side of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's reading explains the חכמים well. But then רבי, who says the lamb is permitted, seems to have no reason. A clear payment to a זונה should be אתנן.

phrases.english: If so,
what is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading of 'slave' as the master himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the payment is for a forbidden relationship with the master, רבי's ruling that it is permitted makes no sense.

steps.title: It really means a slave, an עבד עברי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל בר רב יצחק says the משנה really means 'my slave', but it is talking about a Hebrew slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל בר רב יצחק said: It actually means 'my slave', and the משנה is talking about a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל בר רב יצחק gives a different answer. 'My slave' means a real slave, but a Jewish one, an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This drops רב הונא's 'polite language' reading. Now the case is an עבד עברי, a Jewish slave, and not an עבד כנעני. This gives רבי a reason to permit the lamb. The next step asks how the חכמים can still forbid it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the משנה's case: רב הונא says 'slave' is a polite word for the master, and שמואל בר רב יצחק says it is a real slave, an עבד עברי.

phrases.english: Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
Actually, it means "my slave,"
and when it teaches this, it is about a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם עַבְדִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by replacing רב הונא's reading with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Slave' had to be a polite word for the master, or else the relationship would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a real slave who is an עבד עברי, which explains why רבי permits the lamb.

steps.title: Why would the חכמים forbid it if a Hebrew slave may be with a maidservant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of שמואל בר רב יצחק. If the case is a Hebrew slave, the maidservant is allowed to him, so why would the חכמים call the lamb אתנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the חכמים' reason? A maidservant is fully allowed to a Hebrew slave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that רבי's view now makes sense, but asks how the חכמים can still call the lamb אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 8 explained רבי well: a Hebrew slave may be with a maidservant, so this is not a forbidden relationship. But that same fact seems to break the view of the חכמים, who call the lamb אתנן. אתנן is only payment for a forbidden relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It takes the last answer and shows a problem it causes.
A Jewish (Hebrew) slave who was sold for a set time.

phrases.english: If so, what is the reason of the Rabbis?
A maidservant is fully permitted to a Hebrew slave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 8 from the side of the חכמים' opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל בר רב יצחק's explanation that the משנה is about a Hebrew slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the relationship is allowed, the payment cannot be אתנן, so the חכמים' ruling has no basis.

steps.title: The case is a Hebrew slave who has no wife and children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a Hebrew slave with no wife and children. A ברייתא teaches that a master may not give such a slave a Canaanite maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A slave who has no wife and children. As a ברייתא teaches: if he has no wife and children, his master may not give him a Canaanite maidservant. If he has a wife and children, his master may give him a Canaanite maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case so both opinions make sense, and quotes a ברייתא to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Hebrew slave may only be given a maidservant if he already has a wife and children. In our case he has none, so for the חכמים the relationship is forbidden and the lamb is אתנן. רבי holds the master may give him a maidservant even then, so for him the lamb is not אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? It limits the case to a specific situation.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי and the חכמים is about a Hebrew slave with no wife and children. For the חכמים, the maidservant is forbidden to him, so the lamb is אתנן. For רבי, she is allowed, so it is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long back-and-forth about the lamb given for the maidservant. It shows the two opinions depend on whether a slave with no family may be given a maidservant.

phrases.english: Here, with what case are we dealing?
Such as where he does not have a wife and children,
as it is taught:
If he has no wife and children,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית,
phrases.english: his master may not give him a Canaanite maidservant;
if he has a wife and children,
his master may give him a Canaanite maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a slave without wife and children.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every Hebrew slave may be with a maidservant, so the חכמים have no reason to forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A slave with no wife and children may not be given a maidservant, so for the חכמים the lamb is אתנן.

steps.title: The משנה defines the price of a dog
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה explains what מחיר כלב is: someone trades a lamb for a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is "the price of a dog"? Someone who says to his friend: "Here, take this lamb in place of a dog."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It defines the second forbidden category from the פסוק, מחיר כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids bringing אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב to the בית המקדש. After discussing אתנן, the משנה now explains מחיר כלב. It is an animal given in exchange for a dog, and that animal may not be a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of the משנה text.
The price of a dog: an animal traded for a dog, forbidden as a קרבן.
In place of, in exchange for

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And which is "the price of a dog"?
phrases.notes: This is the phrase from the same פסוק as אתנן, דברים 23:19.

phrases.english: One who says to his friend:
"Here, take this lamb in place of a dog."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the אתנן discussion is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamb given in exchange for a dog is מחיר כלב and may not be brought as a קרבן.

steps.title: Two partners dividing lambs and a dog
steps.stepSummary: Two partners split nineteen lambs and a dog. One takes ten lambs, the other takes nine and the dog. The ten lambs that balance out the dog are forbidden. The nine that go with the dog are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, two partners divided their property. One took ten, and the other took nine and a dog. The ones taken opposite the dog are forbidden, and the ones taken with the dog are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second, less obvious example of מחיר כלב: dividing property between partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partner who took ten lambs took them in place of the dog, so those lambs are like the dog's price. That makes them forbidden. The nine lambs taken together with the dog were not given for the dog, so they stay permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. The ten lambs, taken in exchange for the dog, are the forbidden ones. The nine lambs that came along with the dog are fine.

phrases.english: And likewise, two partners who divided,
one took ten,
and one took nine and a dog,
those taken opposite the dog are forbidden,
phrases.notes: The ten lambs the first partner took in exchange for the other's share, which included the dog.

phrases.english: and those taken with the dog are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case of מחיר כלב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a partnership division, the lambs taken in exchange for the dog are forbidden. The lambs taken with the dog are permitted.

steps.title: Payment for a dog and the price of a prostitute are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the reversed cases are permitted: payment for relations with someone's dog, and an animal paid to buy a prostitute. The פסוק says "two," not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Payment for a dog and the price of a prostitute are permitted, because the פסוק says "two," and not four.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the prohibition to exactly the two cases the פסוק names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב and calls them "both of them." One might think the swapped versions, אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה, are also forbidden. The word "two" teaches that only the two named cases are forbidden, not all four.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given for relations with someone's dog
The price of a prostitute: payment to buy her, for example as a maidservant
Two and not four: only the two cases named in the פסוק are forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: The names are easy to swap. אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב are forbidden. אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה are permitted.

phrases.english: Payment for a dog and the price of a prostitute,
these are permitted,
as it is said "two" and not four.
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19, "both of them" (literally "two").

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶתְנַן הַכֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of the prohibition defined in steps 11-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב are forbidden. The swapped cases are permitted, based on the word "two."

steps.title: The offspring of forbidden animals are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The babies of an animal that is אתנן or מחיר כלב may be brought as קרבנות, because the פסוק says "them" and not their offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring are permitted: the פסוק says "them," and not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more limit: the prohibition does not pass on to the animal's babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "both of them are an abomination." The word "them" points only to the animals themselves. So a lamb born to a forbidden animal may still be a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring, the babies of an animal
"Them" and not their offspring: the word limits the prohibition to the animals themselves.

steps.whatToRemember: Only the actual animal given as אתנן זונה or מחיר כלב is forbidden on the מזבח. The swapped cases and the offspring are all permitted.

phrases.english: Their offspring are permitted:
"them," and not their offspring.
phrases.notes: "Them" is from the same פסוק, דברים 23:19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on the prohibition, alongside step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring of אתנן or מחיר כלב may be offered, based on the word "them."

steps.title: A ברייתא defines מחיר כלב as an animal traded for a dog
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that מחיר כלב means something given in exchange for a dog, not money. It proves this from a פסוק in תהלים where 'price' is used together with 'without wealth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: חכמים taught: 'The price of a dog' means an exchange for a dog. And so the פסוק says: 'You sell Your people without wealth, and have not set their prices high.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that defines מחיר כלב as an animal traded for a dog. It brings a פסוק to show that the word מחיר can mean a trade and not money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תהלים, the people are 'sold' בלא הון, without money, and that is still called מחירהם. So מחיר can mean an item given in a swap. This supports the משנה's case of trading a lamb for a dog.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'price of a dog.' An animal given in exchange for a dog, which may not be brought as a קרבן
Something given in exchange for a dog

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
'The price of a dog': this is an exchange for a dog,
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

phrases.english: and so it says:
'You sell Your people without wealth,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 44:13

phrases.english: 'and have not set their prices high.'
phrases.notes: There was no money involved here, so 'their prices' must mean a swap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from Step 11, which defined מחיר כלב as trading a lamb for a dog.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחיר כלב means an animal given in exchange for a dog. The word מחיר can mean a trade, as shown in תהלים.

steps.title: Maybe מחיר כלב means payment for relations with a dog
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: מחיר כלב could mean real payment, an אתנן, for relations with a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that it means an actual payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reading. Maybe מחיר כלב means payment given for relations with a dog, and not a trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says the word מחיר could simply mean a fee, like an אתנן. If so, the פסוק would be talking about a dog's 'fee' and not a dog trade.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. Used to suggest another reading

phrases.english: Say instead that it is an actual payment,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the round-bracket word 'זונה'; the square-bracket word 'ממש' is the corrected wording. He means a payment for relations with a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition the ברייתא gave in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's definition of מחיר כלב as an exchange for a dog.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מחיר could just as easily mean a payment or fee, so the פסוק might be talking about payment for relations with a dog.

steps.title: That would make three categories, but the פסוק says two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If both kinds of dog payment were included along with אתנן זונה, there would be three forbidden categories. The פסוק says 'both of them,' which means two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there would be three, but the פסוק says 'both of them,' not three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. Adding payment for relations with a dog would make three forbidden categories, but the פסוק counts only two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא assumes the challenger wants to add a category. The list would then be אתנן זונה, אתנן for a dog, and a dog trade. The words גם שניהם limit the list to two.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Both of them.' Words in the פסוק showing there are only two categories

phrases.english: If so, there would be three,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the round-bracket words 'לא קרב,' meaning 'not brought as a קרבן.'

phrases.english: but the פסוק says 'both of them,' and not three!
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 16 using the 'two, not four' idea from Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the payment-to-a-dog case as an extra category on top of the trade.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make three categories, but גם שניהם limits it to two.

steps.title: The challenger explains: replace the trade, don't add to it
steps.stepSummary: The challenger explains that he never meant to add a third category. He meant that מחיר כלב means payment for relations with a dog instead of a trade, so there are still only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did we say payment and also price? We said payment and not price.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger defends his idea. He wants to swap the meaning, not add one, so the count stays at two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'three categories' answer only worked if the trade meaning was kept. If מחיר כלב means only payment for relations with a dog, the two categories are אתנן זונה and payment for a dog. The challenge is back.

keyTerms.meaning: Did we say...? Used to show the other side misunderstood the point

phrases.english: Did we say payment and also price?
We said payment, and not price.
phrases.notes: He means: payment for relations with a dog, and not a trade for a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the challenge of Step 16 against the rejection in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's definition of מחיר כלב as a trade.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read as a replacement, the payment meaning keeps the count at two, so גם שניהם no longer disproves it.

steps.title: The פסוק's different word proves it means a trade
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק meant payment for a dog, it would have said 'אתנן of a prostitute or a dog.' Since it uses a separate word, מחיר, it means something different: an animal traded for a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say: 'Do not bring the payment of a prostitute or a dog.' Since it is written 'the payment of a prostitute and the price of a dog,' learn from this that it means a trade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the wording of the פסוק and proves the ברייתא was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both cases were payment, the פסוק could have used the word אתנן once for both. Instead it uses a second word, מחיר, for the dog. That shows a different kind of transaction, a trade, just as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק say. The פסוק should have been written differently
Learn from this. Used to close a proof

steps.whatToRemember: מחיר כלב means an animal traded for a dog. The proof is that the פסוק uses a separate word, מחיר, and does not just repeat אתנן. Payment for relations with a dog is not included and is permitted, as the משנה taught in Step 13.

phrases.english: If so, let the פסוק say:
'Do not bring the payment of a prostitute or a dog.'
phrases.notes: This is how the פסוק would have looked if both cases were payment. It is not the real wording.

phrases.english: Since it is written 'the payment of a prostitute and the price of a dog,'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

phrases.english: learn from this.
phrases.notes: Learn that מחיר is a different kind of transaction, a trade, just as the ברייתא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed challenge of Step 18 and confirms the ברייתא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the extra wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מחיר כלב might mean payment for relations with a dog.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate word מחיר shows it is a different case, an animal traded for a dog.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מחיר כלב is an animal given in exchange for a dog. Payment for relations with a dog is not included.

steps.title: Quoting the case of partners who divided
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about partners who split their animals, where one took ten lambs and the other took nine lambs and a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: partners who divided their property, one took ten lambs, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a question about it. The question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one partner took ten lambs, and the other took nine lambs plus a dog. The משנה ruled that the ten lambs are forbidden as קרבנות because they were received in exchange for a dog, which is מחיר כלב. The גמרא is about to ask why all ten should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: Partners who divided,
one took, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: one took ten lambs and the other took nine lambs and a dog, so the ten lambs are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of מחיר כלב to a specific case in the משנה that applies it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When partners divide and one gets ten lambs for nine lambs plus a dog, the ten lambs are forbidden as מחיר כלב.

steps.title: Why not forbid just one lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all ten lambs are forbidden. Only one lamb should count as the dog's price, and the rest should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let us set aside one lamb as the payment for the dog, and all the other lambs should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that all ten lambs are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine of the ten lambs were traded for nine lambs, and only the tenth lamb really matches up with the dog. So it seems only one lamb should be מחיר כלב. Why should the dog make all ten forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us take out / set aside

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have this word; the square brackets show it's added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Let us take out one lamb against the dog,
and all those others should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that all ten lambs are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one lamb lines up with the dog. The other nine were traded for nine lambs, so they should be permitted.

steps.title: The dog was worth more than any one lamb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a dog worth more than any single lamb. The extra value is spread over all ten lambs, so every lamb is partly the dog's price.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the dog is worth more than any one of the lambs. That extra value of the dog is spread among all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining which case the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dog were worth exactly one lamb, we could set aside one lamb for it. But here the dog is worth more than any single lamb, so no one lamb can cover its price. The dog's value is spread among all ten lambs, so each lamb is partly מחיר כלב, and all of them are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to explain the specific case being discussed)

steps.whatToRemember: All ten lambs are forbidden because the dog was worth more than any one lamb. Its value is spread across all of them, so each lamb is partly מחיר כלב.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where the value of the dog is more
than any one of them,
and that extra value of the dog
phrases.notes: Some versions say והאי (in round brackets). The corrected wording, in square brackets, is וְהָהוּא. Both mean "that."

phrases.english: is spread among all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן דִּטְפֵי דְּמֵי כֶלֶב מֵחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One lamb could be set aside as the dog's price, leaving the rest permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog is worth more than any single lamb, so its value is spread across all ten, and all are forbidden.

steps.title: Quoting the next ruling: payment for a dog and the price of a prostitute are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה are permitted. Then it introduces רבא מפרזקיא, who is about to ask רב אשי something.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: payment for relations with a dog and the price of a prostitute are permitted, etc. רבא מפרזקיא said to רב אשי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and sets up a discussion about it. The question from רבא מפרזקיא to רב אשי comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the forbidden pair is אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב. Here the משנה says the reverse pair is permitted: an animal paid for relations with a dog, and an animal paid as the price of buying a woman as a maidservant. The line naming רבא מפרזקיא opens a new discussion about this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given for relations with a dog
The price paid for a prostitute (to buy her as a maidservant), not payment for relations

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב are forbidden. The flipped pair, אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה, is permitted.

phrases.english: Payment for a dog and the price of a prostitute
is permitted, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזַקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the partners case to the next ruling in the משנה, which is the reverse of the forbidden pair discussed in steps 15-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal given as payment for relations with a dog, or as the price of buying a prostitute as a maidservant, is permitted as a קרבן.
